name: Cables Wynd House
features: The 'Banana Flats': a long curved slab of 212 deck-access flats over ten storeys in Leith; Category A listed.
note: Built 1962-65; Category A listed in 2017.

name: Preston Bus Station
by: Building Design Partnership (Keith Ingham, Charles Wilson) with Ove Arup & Partners
features: Bus station under a five-storey car park whose curved concrete balconies run the full length; Grade II.
note: Arup chose the curved balcony fronts because flat finishes cost too much. Listed Grade II in 2013.

name: Apollo Pavilion
features: Walk-through sculpture of white in-situ concrete planes bridging a small lake in a new town; Grade II*.
note: Only two files reach 1200px; the rest of the category is 1024px geograph images.

name: Kingsgate Bridge
features: Concrete footbridge on V-shaped legs, built as two halves along the banks and swung 90° to meet; Grade I.
note: Arup's own favourite work; it sits next to Dunelm House (fourth photo shows both).

name: Queen Elizabeth Hall
by: GLC Architects (Hubert Bennett, Jack Whittle, F. G. West, Geoffrey Horsefall)
features: Concert hall and Purcell Room in raw concrete, lifted on columns and laced with raised walkways on the South Bank.

photos.file: File:Queen Elizabeth Hall and Purcell Room.jpg
File:Queen Elizabeth Hall and Purcell Room 2026-03-11.jpg
File:Eastern Side of the Queen Elizabeth Hall.jpg

note: Part of the same South Bank group as the Hayward Gallery (already on the wall). Not listed; renovated 2016-18 by FCB Studios.

name: Brunswick Centre
features: Two long stepped terraces of 560 flats with glazed balconies and service towers, framing a shopping street.
note: Built 1967-72 from studies by Leslie Martin; fell short of its planned size. Grade II listed 2000.

name: Dunelm House
by: Architects' Co-Partnership (Richard Raines, Michael Powers) with Ove Arup
features: Students' union cascading down the River Wear bank; one straight inner 'street' stair links its five levels.

photos.file: File:Dunelm House, University of Durham - geograph.org.uk - 7710190.jpg

note: Listed Grade II in 2021 after the university sought to demolish it. Sits beside Kingsgate Bridge (also in this list). Third photo is from 1967.

name: Institute of Education
features: Long concrete-and-glass block on a raised podium, with tall service towers and stepped ends; only part was built.
commons_category: Category:Exterior of the UCL Institute of Education

photos.file: File:Exterior of the UCL Institute of Education.jpg
File:London MMB M3 University of London Institute of Education.jpg
File:Institute of Education from Russell Square.jpg

note: Built 1970-76 on Bedford Way; Grade II* listed (per Wikipedia's list of brutalist structures). Now UCL's IOE.

name: Wyndham Court
by: Lyons Israel Ellis (E. D. Lyons, Frank Linden, Aubrey Hume)
features: 184 flats over shops in white board-marked concrete, six to seven storeys on a slope, with tall stair towers.

photos.file: File:Wyndham Court, Wyndham Place, Southampton (NHLE Code 1051043) (July 2021) (1).jpg
File:Eastern Wing of Wyndham Court as seen from the South.jpg
File:Wyndham Court, Wyndham Place, Southampton (NHLE Code 1051043) (September 2019).jpg
File:Wyndham Court as approached from Southampton Central Station.jpg

note: Designed 1966, completed 1969; Grade II listed 1998 (Wikipedia's brutalist list says II*).

name: University of East Anglia Ziggurats (Norfolk and Suffolk Terraces)
features: Stepped student residences rising like ziggurats from the meadow above the lake, linked to Lasdun's teaching wall.
commons_category: Category:Suffolk Terrace and Adjoining Walkway and Stairs to Rear, at the University of East Anglia

photos.file: File:Blocks 3 and 4, Suffolk Terrace, UEA - geograph.org.uk - 7982228.jpg
File:Suffolk Terrace (ziggurats), University of East Anglia - geograph.org.uk - 7403857.jpg

note: Two Commons categories: Suffolk Terrace and 'Category:Norfolk Terrace and Attached Walkways, at the University of East Anglia' (fourth photo). Built 1964-68; Grade II* listed.

name: Boston Government Service Center
by: Paul Rudolph (coordinating architect), with Desmond & Lord and Shepley Bulfinch Richardson and Abbott
features: Ribbed 'corduroy' concrete buildings wrapped round a raised plaza, with curving stair towers and deep sunshades.

photos.file: File:Paul Rudolph - Boston Government Services Center (14989170661).jpg

note: Begun 1963, completed 1971; the planned 23-storey tower was never built (a public-domain rendering of it is in the category: File:Boston Government Service Center tower.jpg).

name: J. Edgar Hoover Building
by: C. F. Murphy and Associates (Stanislaw Z. Gladych)
features: FBI headquarters in buff precast concrete: 11 storeys on E Street, 8 on Pennsylvania Avenue, round a trapezoid court.
note: Its future is uncertain: the FBI announced a move out in 2025 and a court blocked it in August 2026 (per Wikipedia).

name: Temple Street Parking Garage
features: Long multi-storey car park of stacked concrete decks on arched, tree-like columns spanning over the street.
note: Designed 1961 (Wikipedia, Paul Rudolph article), opened 1963. No article of its own; form described from the photos.

name: Wurster Hall
by: Joseph Esherick, Vernon DeMars, Donald Olsen
features: Berkeley's architecture school: a raw concrete tower over long wings, its facades hung with deep concrete sunshades.
note: Designed by three faculty members for the College of Environmental Design; renamed Bauer Wurster Hall in 2020. Sunshades described from the photos, not the article.

name: Christian Science Plaza
features: Concrete Colonnade Building, 26-storey tower and Sunday School set round a 210 m reflecting pool.

photos.file: File:Colonnade Building of the First Church of Christ, Scientist.jpg
File:Reflecting Pool at the Christian Science Center in Boston.jpg

note: Most files in the category show the domed Mother Church instead; the chosen ones show Cossutta's 1971-73 buildings and the pool. Third photo is a night view along the colonnade.

name: Institute of Hygiene and Microbiology
features: Free-form research and teaching building in raw concrete, with curving wings, outside stairs and a lecture hall wedge.
commons_category: Category:Institut für Hygiene und Umweltmedizin, Charité Berlin

photos.file: File:Institut für Hygiene und Mikrobiologie Berlin-Lichterfelde 2024-11-21 01.jpg

note: Built 1969-74 for the Free University; listed 2021. Neighbour of the Mäusebunker (already on the wall), across the Teltow Canal. Form words come from the photos.

name: St. Agnes (König Galerie)
by: Werner Düttmann; conversion by Arno Brandlhuber
features: Former church of rough-textured blocks with a square bell tower; converted into an art gallery in 2015.
note: Built 1964-67 as the centre of a social-housing complex; listed. Brandlhuber's 2012-15 conversion won the Berlin Architecture Prize 2016. Type could also be Museum.

name: Schlangenbader Straße Housing (Die Schlange)
by: Georg Heinrichs, Wolf Bertelsmann, Gerhard and Klaus Detlev Krebs
features: 600 m terraced housing block of over 1,000 flats built directly over a motorway tunnel.
note: Built 1973-80 by DEGEWO; listed 2017/18. First photo shows the motorway entering the tunnel under the building. The photos show it painted cream rather than bare concrete, so 'Brutalism' is a loose fit (megastructure).

name: Marl Town Hall
features: Germany's first suspended towers: floors hung from the top of concrete cores, beside a council hall with a folded roof.
note: Competition 1957/58, built 1960-67; two of four planned towers were built. In the SOS Brutalism database.

name: Eastern City Gate (Rudo)
features: Three 28-storey, 85 m housing towers with stepped, tapering profiles, marking the road into Belgrade from the east.

photos.file: File:Источна капија и димњак топлани Коњарник.jpg

note: Built 1973-76. Partner of the Western City Gate (Genex Tower, already on the wall).

name: Macedonian Opera and Ballet
by: Biro 71 (Štefan Kacin, Jurij Princes, Bogdan Spindler, Marjan Uršič)
features: White-painted concrete opera house of sharply folded, asymmetric roof planes, built after the 1963 earthquake.
note: SOS Brutalism dates it 1972-80 and calls it neo-expressionist, hence movement Expressionism; other sources say completed 1979. Some sources call the firm 'Biro 77'.

name: Ruhr University Bochum
features: Campus of 14 near-identical slab blocks, meant as ships in a 'harbour of knowledge', linked by concrete decks.
note: Founded 1962; teaching began 1965 (year given is that opening). Construction of the campus went on into the 1970s. Some blocks are being rebuilt because of PCB contamination.

name: Goce Delčev Student Dormitory
features: Exposed-concrete student towers with projecting service shafts and sky bridges, built in two phases.

photos.file: File:Studentski dom GOCE DELCEV vo Skopje, primer za brutalizam.jpg

note: First section 1969-71, second 1973-77 (SOS Brutalism). Konstantinovski studied at Yale under Paul Rudolph. Blocks renovated 2015-20 after a 2013 fire.

name: House of Soviets
features: Unfinished 21-storey twin-tower block on the old castle site, nicknamed the 'buried robot'; never occupied.
note: DEMOLISHED: demolition began May 2023 and ended August 2024. Construction ran 1970-85 and stopped unfinished, so the year is when work stopped. Owner to decide whether a lost building belongs on the wall.

name: Hotel Thermal
features: Film-festival hotel: a 16-storey slab over a broad podium and a drum-shaped concert hall beside the river.
note: Competition 1963, built 1967-76, opened 1977. Home of the Karlovy Vary film festival; renovation under way since 2019-20.

name: TASS Building
features: News-agency headquarters with deep, round-cornered window frames in sandstone and a globe over the entrance.
note: Completed 1976, headquarters from January 1977. Wikipedia's brutalist list names the architect 'V. S. Egerev'; TASS says Viktor Yegerev.

name: Kotva Department Store
features: Department store built of hexagonal concrete floor modules on 28 braced columns, clad in glass and metal sheet.
note: Built by the Swedish firm SIAB; opened 1975 without its architects, who were by then proscribed. Cultural monument since 2018; under reconstruction until about 2027. Type: no 'Retail' in the vocabulary, so Workplace.

name: Superjednostka
features: 187 m long, 15-storey slab of 762 flats, a Polish take on Le Corbusier's Unité d'Habitation.
note: Built 1967-72. The Unité comparison is the common reading (whitemad, Wikipedia); flats are reached from corridors on every third floor per general sources, not used in the features line.

name: Inter-University Seminar House
features: Main hall shaped as an inverted pyramid 'driven into the earth', with small student houses scattered over the hillside.

photos.file: File:八王子セミナーハウス本館.JPG

note: Main building 1965; the wider campus grew until 1976. Designated Historical Architecture by Tokyo. The 2014 main-building photos are slightly fish-eye.

name: Athénée Français
features: French-language school with sculpted concrete walls, painted in pink and deep purple and pierced by small openings.
note: AIJ Prize winner. Colours described from the photos; the archive dates the project 1960-81 (later additions), Wikipedia gives 1962.

name: Bunkier Sztuki
by: Krystyna Tołłoczko-Różyska; facade by Stefan Borzęcki and Antoni Hajdecki
features: Exhibition pavilion faced in concrete cast from wooden formwork, set into Kraków's old-town ring park.

photos.file: File:Gallery of Contemporary Art “Bunkier Sztuki", 1965 by Krystyna Tołłoczko-Różyska, 3a Szczepański Square, Old Town, Kraków, Poland.jpg
File:Bunkier Sztuki (Bunker of Art) Gallery of Contemporary Art, 3a Szczepański Square, Old Town, Kraków, Poland.jpg

note: Opened 11 September 1965 as the Municipal Exhibition Pavilion; controversial next to the Art Nouveau Palace of Arts. Renovated 2021-24.

name: Imabari City Hall
features: Tange's concrete city hall for his home town, facing his folded-plate public hall across a shared plaza.
note: One of three Tange buildings in Imabari (with the Public Hall, 1958, and Civic Center, 1965); the Public Hall has its own Commons category and could be added. Sources disagree slightly on 1958/1959.

name: Harold Holt Memorial Swimming Centre
features: Brutalist pool hall of chunky wall and stair forms beside Victoria's first heated outdoor 50 m pool.

photos.file: File:Harold Holt Memorial Swimming Pool corner.jpg
File:Harold Holt Memorial Swimming Pool south face.jpg
File:Harold Holt Memorial Swimming Pool entry.jpg

note: Opened March 1969 in Glen Iris; on the Victorian Heritage Register. Named after the prime minister who drowned in 1967.

name: Queensland Art Gallery
features: Low, light-coloured concrete gallery organised along an indoor Watermall, with planted terraces by the river.
commons_category: Category:Exterior of the Queensland Art Gallery

photos.file: File:Queensland Art Gallery river facade, Brisbane.jpg
File:Queensland Art Gallery river facade, Brisbane seen from the bridge.jpg
File:Queensland Art Gallery main entrance, Brisbane.jpg
File:Queensland Art Gallery - Joy of Museums - External.jpg

note: First stage of Gibson's Queensland Cultural Centre (Wikipedia's brutalist list names the centre, 1985). State Heritage Place 2015.

name: Cameron Offices
features: Office wings of precast post-tensioned concrete off an in-situ concrete mall, linked by a bridge over the avenue.
note: PARTLY DEMOLISHED: wings 1, 2 and 6-10 removed in 2007-08; wings 3-5 and the bridge survive (Commonwealth Heritage List 2005), two now student housing.

name: Golden Mile Complex
by: Design Partnership (Gan Eng Oon, William Lim, Tay Kheng Soon)
features: 16-storey mixed-use block with a stepped, terraced section: flats over a shopping podium, facing the sea.
note: Gazetted for conservation in 2021; being refurbished as 'The Golden Mile' with a new 45-storey tower beside it (due 2029). Photos are 2005-07 and only 1600px.

name: Joseph Regenstein Library
features: Library of grooved limestone in stacked vertical fins that read like concrete, on the site of Stagg Field.

photos.file: File:Regenstein Library, University of Chicago, 57th Street and Ellis Avenue, Hyde Park, Chicago, IL (54514265602).jpg
File:Regenstein Library, University of Chicago, 57th Street and Ellis Avenue, Hyde Park, Chicago, IL (54514267557).jpg

note: Opened 1970 where the first controlled nuclear chain reaction took place (1942). Fourth photo shows it beside Helmut Jahn's glass-domed Mansueto Library.

name: Scarborough College (Andrews Building)
features: Two wings meet at a central atrium; wide indoor 'streets' with balconies keep students out of the winter.

photos.file: File:Humanities Wing at U of T Scarborough.jpg
File:Science Wing at U of T Scarborough.jpg

note: Andrews disliked the 'brutalist' label, saying the design came from human needs and logic. Commons also has Category:Humanities Wing and Category:Science Wing.

name: Miami Marine Stadium
features: Concrete grandstand for 6,566 under a cantilevered folded-plate roof on eight slanted columns, facing a boat basin.
note: Only one good free photo found (no Commons category of its own; architect's category is Category:Hilario Candela). Designed by Candela at 28; closed after Hurricane Andrew (1992), on the National Register since 2018, restoration begun 2023.

name: Slovak National Gallery Extension
by: Vladimír Dedeček; renovation by Architekti BKPŠ
features: Long gallery wing lifted on piers like a bridge (the 'Overbridge') in front of the older gallery buildings.
note: Designed 1963-69, built 1969-77; reopened December 2022 after a seven-year renovation by BKPŠ. More files in the category ('SNG, predná časť' series, 2016-era) were not viewed.

name: University Hall, University of Lethbridge
features: 912 ft, nine-storey concrete block laid along the coulees above the Oldman River like the nearby rail viaduct.
note: Built 1969-71; teaching and student rooms in one structure. Length and storeys come from one university archive notice only. Many category files are interiors.

name: National Arts Centre
features: Performing-arts centre in reinforced concrete, planned on interlocking hexagons and triangles beside the Rideau Canal.
note: Opened June 1969 (some sources say 31 May). A glass addition by Diamond Schmitt (2017) now fronts Elgin Street; the chosen photos show mostly the original concrete. National Historic Site.

name: Hillbrow Tower (Telkom Joburg Tower)
by: South African Posts & Telecommunications (client); designers not credited in sources
features: 269 m concrete telecom tower, Africa's tallest, with public floors and a revolving restaurant near the top.
note: No source found naming the architect or engineer; 'by' needs filling before it goes on the wall. Built 1968-71; public floors closed since 1981.

name: Most SNP (UFO Bridge)
by: Arpád Tesár, Jozef Lacko, Ivan Slameň
features: Asymmetric cable-stayed bridge with a 303 m span hung from one leaning A-pylon, topped by a saucer-shaped restaurant.

photos.file: File:Puente de la Insurrección Nacional Eslovaca, Bratislava, Eslovaquia, 2020-02-01, DD 49.jpg

note: Built 1967-72; 84.6 m pylon. A steel structure rather than raw concrete, but it appears in Wikipedia's list of brutalist structures and is a key work of the period. Movement could also be Late modernism.

name: National Carillon
features: 50 m concrete bell tower of three tall shafts on an island in Lake Burley Griffin, housing 57 bells.

photos.file: File:Canberra Carillon on Lake Burley Griffin-2 (38441217986).jpg
File:Carillon Viewed from National Gallery of Australia Gardens.jpg

note: Opened by Queen Elizabeth II on 26 April 1970. The three shafts stand for the British and Australian governments and the City of Canberra. Bells by John Taylor & Co.

name: Majdanek Mausoleum
features: 35 m concrete dome raised on three supports over a bowl of victims' ashes, at the end of a 1.3 km memorial road.
note: Part of the Monument of Struggle and Martyrdom at the former Majdanek concentration camp (1967 competition, unveiled 1969). Frieze: 'Let our fate be a warning to you.' Sensitive site: present with care. Restored 2023-25.

name: Orange County Government Center
features: County offices and courts as a cluster of interlocking concrete boxes with 87 roofs round a courtyard.
note: No usable free exterior photo: the category has only small files (500px) and one wide 'during demolition' shot (File:Orange County Government Center during demolition.jpg, 6048x2160, CC BY-SA 3.0). Form too intricate to draw with confidence. Centre section demolished 2015; rebuilt and reopened 2017.
